clue.text: Stupid of setter having nothing to offer solvers?

definitions.meaning: stupid means lacking any idea or understanding

definitions.text: of setter having nothing to offer solvers?
definitions.meaning: a setter with nothing to give solvers would be without a clue, read as clue plus the suffix meaning without

explanation.surface: A solver grumbles that the setter is foolish to give them nothing to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into CLUE and LESS: a setter offering solvers no clue is literally without one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without a clue is the idiom for being dim or ignorant, so it is a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Face being lifted out of bed, incapacitated

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a facelift is stuck in bed, unable to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being lifted' turns DIAL upwards in this down clue, giving LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A person laid up is confined, usually to bed, by illness or injury, so out of action.

clue.text: Suppress certain novel ideas

indicators.note: certain means some of, so only some letters of novel ideas are used, running across the two words

parts.note: novel means new, so the letters of the following word are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A censor stifles certain original thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the anagram signal for IDEAS, but 'certain' says some of the letters of 'novel ideas' are taken as they stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit or pass over something, as a sound in speech, so it can mean suppress.

clue.text: Bride hung around festival location

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so the letters of the two words are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride is left waiting at the spot where a festival is held.
explanation.walkthrough: EDINBURGH is the Scottish capital, home of the famous August arts festival and Fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish capital hosts the world's largest arts festival each August, so it is a festival venue.

clue.text: Cat seems out to adopt independent attitude initially

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside another
out means wrong or disordered, so the word seems is rearranged
initially means the first letters of the words independent and attitude are taken

explanation.surface: A cat seems to take on an aloof, independent air, as cats are known for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives SMESE; 'to adopt' looks like taking in a pet, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic cat from Thailand, so this is an example of a cat.

clue.text: Scientist caught replacing black box

indicators.note: one letter replacing another means it takes the other's place in the word

parts.note: boffin is British slang for a scientist or researcher
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A scientist recovers a flight's black box after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts C where the B of BOFFIN was. 'Black box' looks like one item, but black belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin is the box in which a body is buried, so box is a fair informal synonym.

clue.text: Young archer's tooth surgeon at first extracted

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, as a tooth is, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a cuspid is a canine tooth

indicators.note: at first means the first letter of surgeon is taken

explanation.surface: A young archer has a tooth pulled by a dental surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a contraction of 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is shown as a winged boy with a bow, shooting arrows at lovers.

clue.text: Jellied eggs man undersells, left out for restaurant originally

indicators.note: one letter out for another means it is swapped out and the other put in its place

parts.note: to flog goods is to sell them cheaply

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of restaurant is taken

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man

explanation.surface: A man cuts his prices on jellied eggs, but his restaurant drops them from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for' swaps the L of FLOGS for R, from 'originally', giving FROGS.
explanation.definitionFit: The eggs of frogs are laid in masses held in a clear jelly, so they are jellied eggs.

clue.text: Where a batsman starts to advance

definitions.meaning: a cricket batsman begins an innings standing at the crease, the line marked on the pitch
to advance is to grow or go up in amount

explanation.surface: A cricket question: where does a batsman take his first step forward?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line where the batsman stands, so a batsman starts 'in crease'.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance as a verb means to rise or grow, a direct synonym of going up in amount.

clue.text: Cycling briefly towards Indonesia's capital in swimwear

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: biking is cycling

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first letter, so the first letter of Indonesia's is taken

explanation.surface: A cyclist briefly heads to Indonesia's capital wearing only swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Jakarta, but it means the first letter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit for women is a bikini, a type of swimwear.

clue.text: Method followed by bagpiper regularly gets instructor scratching head

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of bagpiper, starting from the second
scratching means striking out, so the head, or first letter, is removed

parts.note: a coach is an instructor or trainer

explanation.surface: A bagpiper's method leaves his instructor scratching his head in puzzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' looks like puzzlement but removes the first letter, leaving OACH.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach is a way of tackling a problem, so it is a synonym for a method.

clue.text: Important businesswoman's card placed in front of worker

indicators.note: placed in front of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a queen is a playing card
a worker is a bee, the commonest kind in a hive

explanation.surface: A businesswoman's business card sits in front of one of her staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a contraction of 'is'. 'Worker' is a crossword staple for BEE or ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominant woman at the top of a group is called a queen bee, after the ruling insect of the hive.

clue.text: Film-maker does not broadcast in Glasgow

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: Scots say disnae for does not

explanation.surface: A film-maker's work is not shown in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Glasgow' says the words are Scottish: DISNAE is Scots for doesn't, and it sounds like DISNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Disney was the American animator and studio founder who made Snow White and Bambi.

clue.text: Israeli male misbehaving outside Calais terminal — do the French stand for it?

definitions.text: do the French stand for it?

indicators.note: outside means the first piece is placed around the second
misbehaving means acting out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
terminal means the end, so the last letter of Calais is taken

explanation.surface: An Israeli man behaves badly outside the Calais ferry terminal, testing French patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges ISRAELI MALE into MAREILLAISE, and 'outside' puts it round S, from 'terminal', after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: La Marseillaise is the French national anthem, for which French people rise to their feet.

clue.text: Substitute meat with fish soup, kilo being consumed

indicators.note: being consumed means eaten up, so one letter goes inside the other piece
soup suggests a mixture, so the letters of meat and fish are stirred together

explanation.surface: A recipe swaps meat for fish in a soup, with a kilo eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' gives MAESHIFT; 'Substitute' reads as a verb in the surface but defines an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is a temporary stand-in, used for want of the real thing.

clue.text: Fruit drink derived from broadleaf tree sap?

parts.note: the lime, or linden, is a broadleaved tree
sap is the juice of a plant

explanation.surface: A drink is supposedly made by tapping a tree's sap.
explanation.walkthrough: The lime tree, or linden, is not the citrus that gives the drink: the surface plays on the two limes.
explanation.definitionFit: The juice of the citrus fruit, drunk by sailors against scurvy, is a fruit drink.

clue.text: Reduce extent of Northern Irish territory

indicators.note: the size of Down puts the county's name before the size

parts.note: Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
extent means size

explanation.surface: A proposal to shrink the area of a Northern Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, south-east of Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To downsize is to make smaller, especially a workforce or home, so it is a synonym of reduce.

clue.text: Alan Bennett perhaps I rank more shy by mistake

indicators.note: by mistake means put wrongly, so the letters of the four words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Alan Bennett muses that he has been wrongly ranked as more shy than he is.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Bennett is a playwright from Leeds, in the English county of Yorkshire, famed for his shy, wry persona.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett was born and raised in Leeds, so he is an example of a man from that northern county.

clue.text: Love Italian church building from Cremona

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lover admires an Italian church built in Cremona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building from Cremona' adds a second route: CREMONA rearranged gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, so love here is the relationship itself.

clue.text: Thoughtful American sacked 12 possibly

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so the letters are thrown out

parts.note: studious means thoughtful and given to study
US stands for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: A thoughtful American has been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 points to the answer at 12 across, the film-maker; 'possibly' says this is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney is a film company, so it is an example of a film studio.

clue.text: New po-faced Welsh Assembly member is ousted

indicators.note: is ousted means is thrown out, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: po-faced means stern and humourless, unamused
AM was the title Assembly Member, used in the Welsh Assembly

explanation.surface: A newly elected, stony-faced Welsh Assembly member is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: AM, Assembly Member, was the title of members of the Welsh Assembly before it became the Senedd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never used is still fresh and in mint condition, so it is new.

clue.text: Impulse to take to the road

definitions.meaning: an impulse is an urge or motivating force
to take to the road in a car is to steer it along

explanation.surface: Someone feels the urge to set off on a road trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun is an inner urge; as a verb it is to operate a car on the road.

clue.text: Those standing hope it will be comfortable for them

definitions.text: Those standing hope it will be comfortable for them

parts.words: Those standing hope it will be comfortable for them
parts.note: election candidates standing for office hope to win by a comfortable margin of votes

explanation.surface: People on their feet hope for a comfortable experience, like a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' means standing for election, not on one's feet; a comfortable win is the hope.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning candidate's margin of votes over the rest is what they hope will be comfortable.

clue.text: Interest obtained from French bank over time

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece over another means it comes first

parts.note: rive is French for a river bank

explanation.surface: A saver earns interest from a French bank over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial beside 'bank', but it is the verb: to hold someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet someone is to hold their attention completely, so it is to interest them.

clue.text: Image of princess generates formal vote in Parliament

indicators.note: a vision of Di puts the princess before the image

parts.note: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales
a vision is an image

explanation.surface: A picture of a princess prompts a formal vote among MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons, a division is a vote in which members file into separate lobbies to be counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament splits into two lobbies to count votes, so a division is its formal vote.

clue.text: Overrun of report attacked in speech

indicators.note: of report means as reported or spoken, so the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: to inveigh is to protest angrily in words, so attacked in speech is inveighed

explanation.surface: A report of an overrun is attacked in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: To inveigh is to speak out in angry protest, so INVEIGHED means attacked in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To invade is to enter and occupy territory by force, so it is to overrun it.

clue.text: Rage she felt now and then towards empty house

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so alternate letters are taken, starting with the first
empty means the middle is removed, leaving only the outer letters of house

explanation.surface: She felt a pang of resentment towards an empty house.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, like a liquid churning near the boil, a synonym of rage.

clue.text: Exercise sanction when only outside-halves are showing effort

indicators.note: the outside halves are the first half of the first word and the second half of the second word
showing means visible, so the end half of sanction is what remains in view

explanation.surface: A rugby coach sanctions exercise when only the fly-halves turn up for training.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside-half is rugby's name for fly-half. Here 'only outside-halves are showing' keeps the first half of Exercise and the last half of sanction.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion is physical or mental effort, the expending of energy.
